raw_response:
I will not start from zero. I will start from what has worked for me on irrigated land here in southern Hebei and then adjust a little for cost, labor, and yield. I have 16.1 mu total, only 2 people at home, and I cannot spread myself too thin in peak season, so I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize system and leave a smaller block for cotton. I will put 10.0 mu into wheat-maize and 6.1 mu into cotton. With my education and these years of farming, I look at it as output per mu and risk per mu. Wheat and maize on irrigated land are still the steady part of the income, so I will not save money too hard on fertilizer there. If nitrogen is short, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. For wheat I will feed enough base fertilizer and then topdress once around jointing, with 2 irrigations because I have well water. For summer maize after wheat, I will keep it simple and efficient, use hybrid seed, more nitrogen than phosphorus, one irrigation if rain is poor, and fewer passes because labor is tight. Cotton I will keep on the smaller area because it needs more watching and more spraying, but I will still plant it because spread risk matters. I will not push cotton fertilizer as hard as maize, but I will keep potassium up and spray more often because insects can ruin the field quickly. My whole plan is to hold steady yield first, control labor second, and only then squeeze input costs.
